answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds cryptographic stake burning to identity creation, scaling required burn costs superlinearly by O(N^2) per cluster. An attacker faces exponential resource depletion when forging identities, as each transaction log signed by a cryptographic quill imposes an unrecoverable toll. Like burning dense timber or smelting rigid ferrous ore, this irreversible expenditure guarantees attacking costs vastly outpace potential coordination profits.
